title: Company-wide policies and processes
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees and managers to ensure consistent, compliant behavior across teams.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who access company systems, purchase on behalf of the company, manage customer data, or travel on behalf of Redwood. Specific teams (security, finance-legal, people-ops) retain policy ownership for their sections as noted.

1) Access & Permissions

Principles
- Principle of least privilege: grant the minimum required access for the shortest practical duration.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is the default; attribute-based access where necessary.
- All elevated access requests must be justified, time-bound, and approved by the resource owner.

Standard Roles and Ownership
- Admin (full config, billing): cloud-accounts-and-networking team
- Service Owner: each product/service team (declared in team wiki)
- Developer: standard dev access to non-production environments
- On-call SRE: elevated runbook and incident tools access

Requesting Access (Step-by-step)
1. Submit a request via the Access Portal (Confluence link + internal form). Include: requested role, scope, justification, expiration date.
2. Resource owner reviews within 3 business days.
3. Security performs an automated policy check and authorizes or flags for manual review.
4. Provisioning executed via IAM automation (Terraform / SCIM integration).

Temporary & Emergency Access
- Temporary access <= 30 days: allowed with owner approval and automated expiration.
- Emergency access (SEV>2 incident): on-call SRE can grant emergency elevation; log and retro-review required within 72 hours.

Periodic Review
- Quarterly access certification: team leads must review active grants; flagged accounts >30 days unused are disabled.

2) Change Management

Change Types
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-approved (e.g., routine config updates).
- Normal change: planned changes with impact analysis and scheduled window.
- Emergency change: required to restore service or mitigate security incidents.

Change Lifecycle
1. Request (Change Request ticket in Change Board JIRA) — include owner, risk, rollback plan, monitoring playbook.
2. Review (Change Advisory Board - CAB) — weekly for normal changes.
3. Approval — for changes affecting SLAs or production, at least one engineering owner and one security/finance sign-off required.
4. Schedule — changes should target approved maintenance windows (see table below).
5. Execute — follow runbooks, use feature flags/canaries for rollouts.
6. Post-change review — update runbooks and incident trackers if any anomalies.

Maintenance windows (default)
- Low-impact: Weekdays 02:00–04:00 PT
- High-impact: Saturday 03:00–07:00 PT (pre-approved by SRE and product owners)

Emergency Change Process
- Initiate emergency JIRA with prefix EMG-; notify CAB and on-call Slack channel.
- Implement with owner and SRE oversight.
- Conduct RCA and change review within 5 business days.

3) Data Management

Data Classification
- Public: data intended for public consumption.
- Internal: internal business information without PII/sensitive details.
- Confidential: PII, customer data, or legal/regulatory data.
- Restricted: highly sensitive (PHI, regulated financial data).

Handling Requirements (by classification)
- Public: no special handling.
- Internal: encrypted at rest optional; access on need-to-know basis.
- Confidential: encrypted at rest and in transit (TLS 1.2+), access logged, retention policy enforced.
- Restricted: must be stored in approved environments (Private deployment or customer-dedicated) with KMS/HSM-backed keys.

Retention & Deletion
- Default retention for customer-owned data: 7 years unless contract states otherwise.
- Retention for logs: operational logs 90 days, audit logs 2 years (unless longer retention purchased).
- Deletion requests follow the Data Subject Request (DSR) playbook (Security & Legal).

Backups & Recovery
- Nightly backups for critical services, tested quarterly.
- RTO/RPO targets declared per service in the service catalog.

Encryption & Key Management
- All customer and confidential data must be encrypted at rest with company-managed KMS. For private deployments, customer-managed KMS is preferred.

Data Transfers & Third Parties
- Cross-border transfers require legal review if customer data is Confidential/Restricted.
- Vendor data access must be limited to approved scopes and logged.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Principles
- Competitive procurement for contracts > $50k.
- Clear cost-center assignment and PO generation for purchases.
- Individuals must not commit company to contractual obligations without procurement/finance approval.

Purchase Flow (summary)
1. Raise a Purchase Request in Procurement Portal with justification, budget code, and requested vendor.
2. Procurement performs vendor checks (security questionnaire, financials) for new vendors.
3. Finance issues PO and routes to vendor.
4. Receipts/invoices submitted to AP for payment.

Approval Matrix
- <= $2,000: Team lead approval
- $2,001–$25,000: Manager + Finance approval
- $25,001–$50,000: Director + Finance approval
- > $50,000: VP + Procurement and Legal review

Expense Reimbursement
- Employees submit via Expense tool with receipts within 30 days.
- Travel expenses must include purpose, approver, and itemized receipts.
- Per diem rates and pre-approval rules in travel section.

5) Vendor Management

Onboarding Checklist
- Business justification and owner.
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed by Security team.
- Contract with SLAs, termination clauses, and data processing addenda (DPA) if handling customer data.
- PO/Invoice flow setup with Finance.

Ongoing Oversight
- Quarterly vendor reviews for strategic vendors; annual security revalidation for vendors with Confidential/Restricted access.
- Contract renewal reminders generated 90/60/30 days before expiry.

Termination & Offboarding
- Revoke all access, collect assets, and validate data deletion/return per contract.
- Run a final audit within 10 business days of contract end.

6) Travel Policies

Booking & Approvals
- All business travel requires pre-approval from manager. International travel requires People Ops and Security notification for high-risk regions.
- Use approved travel vendors for booking (company travel portal).

Allowable Expenses
- Airfare: economy for domestic; premium economy for flights >8 hours with manager approval.
- Lodging: mid-range business hotels; exceptions require manager pre-approval.
- Meals: per diem or receipt-based reimbursement; refer to country-specific per diem table.

Safety & Insurance
- Company provides business travel insurance for approved trips. Register trips in the Travel Safety tool.
- Emergency contact procedures and evacuation support available through People Ops.

7) Internal Templates and Resources

Quick links and templates (stored in Templates space):
- Access Request Form: /confluence/templates/access-request-form
- Change Request Template (JIRA): /confluence/templates/change-request
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist: /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding
- Purchase Request Form: /confluence/templates/purchase-request
- Expense Report Template: /confluence/templates/expense-report
- Data Handling Checklist: /confluence/templates/data-handling-checklist

Template usage notes
- Always make a local copy before editing; template updates are managed by People Ops and Procurement.
- Fill required fields (owner, cost center, justification) to avoid delays.

Governance, Escalation & Contacts
- Policy owner: People Ops (Maya Thompson, maya@redwood.com) — responsible for cross-policy alignment.
- Security owner (data & vendor security): Ethan Chen, security@redwood.com
- Procurement & Finance: Priya Desai, procurement@redwood.com
- Incident & Change Board contact: eng-sre@redwood.com

Exceptions and Policy Changes
- Exceptions require documented risk assessment, approval by policy owner and at least one senior representative from Security or Finance depending on the domain.
- Policy updates follow the in_review -> published workflow with reviewers and a 7-day comment period before publishing.

Appendix A — Change Risk Matrix (example)
| Impact | Likelihood | Risk Level | Approver |
|--------|------------|------------|----------|
| Low | Unlikely | Low | Team Lead |
| Medium | Possible | Medium | Engineering Manager + Security |
| High | Likely | High | Director + Security + Product |

Appendix B — Contact & Escalation Summary
- General policy questions: people-ops@redwood.com
- Procurement questions: procurement@redwood.com
- Security & data questions: security@redwood.com
